customManagers.description: The single ansible-core pin used by the hardware job, which must stay compatible with the lab runner's Python 3.10. This is the only ansible-core version Renovate can meaningfully manage here: the sanity and unit matrices are comma-separated LISTS of supported versions, not single pins, so there is no 'current version' for Renovate to bump. Widening or narrowing that support matrix is a deliberate policy decision -- the Dependency Dashboard will still surface new ansible-core releases for a human to act on.

packageRules.description: ansible-core is the collection's compatibility contract, not an ordinary dependency. meta/runtime.yml declares a floor, the sanity/unit matrices enumerate versions, and the hardware job is constrained by the lab runner's Python. A bump here is a deliberate support-policy decision, so it gets its own PR and never automerges.
prBodyNotes: :warning: Raising or dropping an ansible-core version is a support-policy change. Before merging, check: `meta/runtime.yml` requires_ansible floor; the sanity and unit matrices in `.circleci/config.yml`; whether `tests/sanity/ignore-*.txt` files need adding or removing; and whether the module boilerplate requirement changed (it changed incompatibly at 2.17). The hardware job is separately constrained by the lab runner's Python version.

packageRules.description: cimg/python images in the CI matrix. Safe to group, but a new Python minor still needs a matrix entry to actually be tested, so review rather than automerge.
Runtime dependency. Deliberately just requests -- see requirements.txt for why lxml is avoided. Patch and minor bumps are low risk and the unit suite covers the transport thoroughly.
Test-only dependencies. Grouped and automerged on green CI, since a regression here can only break the test run, and the run is what gates it.
